AmaFiora Review

Review of AmaFiora

The 2027-built AmaFiora cruise ship is deployed on the Rhine and Moselle rivers and the Dutch and Belgian inland waterways, departing from homeports Amsterdam (Netherlands) and Basel/Zurich (Switzerland)

The vessel (ENI number tba) will be Switzerland-flagged (MMSI 269057135) and registered in Basel.

AmaFiora is AmaWaterways' 25th boat and the 15th from the modified Concerto-class.

The 152-passenger AmaFiora is part of AmaWaterways' modified Concerto-class fleet, whose sisterships are AmaKristina (2016), AmaViola (2016), AmaStella (2016), AmaLea (2018), AmaMora (2019), AmaSiena (2020), AmaLucia (2021), and AmaSofia (2026).

Decks and Cabins

AmaFiora's 76 staterooms are across 10 categories and include 4 Twin Balcony Suites, 45 Twin Balcony Staterooms, 18 French Balcony cabins, and 9 Riverview cabins (with non-opening high windows).

Most staterooms feature AmaWaterways' signature Twin Balcony design and measure 20-22 m2 (210-235 ft2). The four Suites are the largest accommodations, measuring 33 m2 (350 ft2).

Standard cabin amenities include a hotel-style Queen (double bed convertible to twin beds) luxury bedding sets, under-bed suitcase storage, ample closet space, bedside cabinets with drawers and reading lamps, two long-range portable audio devices (for use during land tours and excursions), individual climate control, a private bathroom (single-sink vanity, glass-door shower, hairdryer, premium bath amenities, bathrobes), digital safe (in the closet), direct-dial phone, TV, and daily-supplied complimentary bottled water.

Mini-bars are available in Twin Balcony staterooms only.

Free shipwide Wi-Fi is also included.

The boat has 4 decks, of which 3 have cabins.

Shipboard facilities and amenities

All AmaWaterways ships provide complimentary bicycles, stored on the sundeck, for guests to use during shore excursions and tours at each port of call along the cruise itinerary.

A passenger elevator/lift connects only two cabin decks (Cello/2nd/, and Violin/3rd).

Next are reviewed the AmaFiora ship's venues, facilities, and amenities by deck.

Piano Deck (1st floor)

The wellness complex consists of a Spa (two Massage Rooms for body massages and facial treatments) and a Gym/Fitness Room. All rooms have floor-to-ceiling windows.

The ship has no Beauty Salon/Hair Salon (hairstyling and barber services, manicure and pedicure) and Sauna.

On the Piano Deck are also all staff and crew cabins.

Cello Deck (2nd floor)

Journeys Restaurant (Main Dining Room) is the ship's primary dining venue serving breakfast, lunch, and a 3-course dinner, all included in the cruise fare. The dining room is spacious, with modern furnishings, comfortable upholstered chairs, luxury dining amenities (premium table linens, china, cutlery, glassware), and large wall-to-wall and floor-to-ceiling windows offering river views from nearly every table. Tables are arranged for couples as well as larger groups (up to 8 guests per table). Meals are primarily waiter-served, although breakfast and lunch also include buffet components. Complimentary beverages (regional wines, beer, and soft drinks) are served with lunch and dinner.

Adjacent to the Restaurant is the Galley (kitchen and storage rooms for provisions). It supports two dining venues simultaneously (Journeys Restaurant, Al Fresco). Food preparation emphasizes fresh regional ingredients and daily baking. Special dietary requirements are generally accommodated when requested before sailing.

Violin Deck (3rd floor)

The fore-located Bow Terrace is a great vantage point for outdoor observation. The space is accessed from the Al Fresco.

The Lark Lounge & Bar is the ship's main social venue, featuring floor-to-ceiling and wall-to-wall windows, a full-service bar, comfortable lounge seating, a dance floor, a grand piano and live musical/show performances (in the afternoons and evenings), and a large screen used for lectures/media presentations and evening entertainment. Standard cocktails, premium spirits, specialty wines, and premium beverages may incur additional charges, while many drinks are included depending on the fare and service period. The lounge's evening programming includes live music and vocal performances, cocktail hour (nightly), a live show program with local performers (dancers and musicians boarding the riverboat), and the crew show (once per cruise). The daily programming includes various workshops, classes, demonstrations, trivia games, and watching movies. Special activities hosted here are themed dance nights and food-and-wine tastings (itinerary-based / local delicacies, liqueurs, cheeses, sweets, etc).

Al Fresco is a bow-facing, glass-enclosed dining venue with direct access from the Lark Lounge. It is also accessed via outside stairs from the Sun Deck (above). Al Fresco serves breakfast and lunch, and features floor-to-ceiling glass walls. Depending on weather, sections may open for fresh air while remaining protected from wind. Meals are included in the cruise fare and generally feature lighter buffet selections than the main restaurant.

The Lobby Hall (Atrium's upper level) houses the ship entrances (portside and starboard), the Boutique, and the Reception Desk (24-hour general assistance, information, account queries, purser services, key-card issues). The Reception doubles as the Cruise Director's Office, providing information on shore excursions/tours, daily scheduled activities, and also serving AmaWaterways' onboard cruise booking program.

In the Lobby, there is also a complimentary (open 24 hours) self-service beverage station offering coffee, espresso-based drinks from automated machines, hot water, tea bags, hot chocolate, and occasional cookies or pastries. Guests don't need a drink package to use the station.

Boutique is a small Shop selling mainly locally made gifts and souvenirs, AmaWaterways-logoed merchandise, and travel essentials.

The Chef's Table is a 24-seat specialty restaurant. The dining experience is included in the fares, with every passenger receiving one reservation per cruise. The aft-facing restaurant has floor-to-ceiling windows for stern views (of the ship's wake) and features a live cooking experience/an open kitchen where guests can watch the chefs prepare each course. The dinner menu is a multi-course tasting menu with carefully selected regional wine pairings. The Chef's Table menus change seasonally, with most dishes prepared with fresh locally-sourced ingredients. Vegetarian, vegan, and other dietary preferences are accommodated with advance notice. The dinner lasts about 2 hours, allowing guests to enjoy each course at a leisurely pace. The chefs explain the dishes, the wine pairings are thoughtfully chosen, and the overall presentation rivals that of many land-based fine restaurants.

Sun Deck (4th floor)

The bow-facing Sun Deck & The Deck Club (fka Lower Sun Deck) is an open-air lounge/seating area and offers unique vantage points for enjoying the riverside scenery. The Deck Club features comfortable shaded seating (sofas and chairs) and 4-seat tables. Beverage service is provided from the Al Fresco Lounge (below) accessed via outside stairs.

Forward-midship is the Navigation Bridge (Wheelhouse) and the bicycle stands. Next is the sunbathing area with a heated freshwater pool and a swim-up bar. The sundeck area is furnished with luxury loungers and deckchairs. The shaded seating areas are covered by retractable awnings and are encircled by a Walking Track.

On select days, an alfresco lunch is served, while each morning (depending on weather), an open-air group exercise class is organized (complimentary activity).

All sundeck structures (Wheelhouse, awnings, glass railings) are collapsible and lowered when the ship passes under low bridges. During these periods, the Sun Deck closes temporarily, all furniture is secured, and passengers must leave the deck until clearance is restored.

Itineraries

AmaFiora's inaugural cruise schedule (2027-2028) listed the following themed itineraries:

  • (Dutch & Belgian Waterways) BEST OF HOLLAND & BELGIUM is a 7-night roundtrip from Amsterdam visiting the Netherlands and Belgium. TULIP TIME is another 7-night roundtrip from Amsterdam.
  • (Rhine & Moselle Rivers) CAPTIVATING RHINE is a 7-night voyage between Amsterdam and Basel that visits France, Germany, the Netherlands, and Switzerland. The reverse route (Basel to Amsterdam) is titled ENCHANTING RHINE.
  • The B2B cruise (14-night itinerary Amsterdam-Basel-Amsterdam) is titled GRAND RHINE & DUCH CANALS.

AmaFiora also offers two-ship cruisetours that combine the Rhine cruise with a Seine cruise in France. The 21-night itinerary is themed GRAND EUROPEAN MEDLEY and runs between Basel and Paris, with included train travel. The 14-night cruisetour is titled GRAND SEINE & DUTCH IMPRESSIONS.

The holiday-themed itinerary is titled CHRISTMAS MARKETS ON THE RHINE (7-night, between Basel and Amsterdam).

Themed Wine Cruises feature guest lectures by renowned wine experts and onboard tastings.

AmaFiora cruise packages include complimentary Wi-Fi, all tours and excursions (including guided bike tours), ground transfers, live evening entertainment with local performers, daily enrichment lectures, wine and food tastings, 24-hour coffee and tea service, and replenished bottled water in cabins.

AmaFiora cruise prices are per person, based on double occupancy, and are indicative only. Actual fares may vary depending on promotional offers, group bookings, and last-minute deals. AmaWaterways also offers discounted airfare packages with major airlines, without charging flight deviation fees.

AmaFiora Wiki

The boat is named after Kruzof Island, part of the Alexander Archipelago in southeastern Alaska, located approximately 16 km (10 mi) west of Sitka, AK. The island was originally named San Jacinto, later St. Hyacinthe (1775) and Pitt Island (1787). The Russians subsequently referred to it as Sitka Island, Edgecumbe Island, and Crooze-Kruzow-Kruzof. Kruzof Island measures 39 km (24 mi) in length and 14 km (9 mi) in width, with a total land area of about 434 km² (167.5 mi²). Its highest point, Mount Edgecumbe, rises to 976 m (3,201 ft).

The charter yacht Royal Pelagic accommodated up to 17 passengers and 9 crew. Onboard amenities included dedicated entertainment and leisure facilities, alfresco dining (lunch and dinner) on the open deck, sunbathing areas, and watersports equipment. Powered by engines delivering a cruising speed of 10 knots (maximum 11 knots / 13 mph / 20 km/h), the yacht had an operational range of 13,819 nautical miles (15,900 mi / 25,600 km) with fuel tank capacity of 40,000 US gallons (151,400 L).
